provenance.what: the scale-resolved planetary morphology evidence atlas
provenance.principle: Every number that appears in more than one record is read from both and reconciled here. One disagreement and this file is not written.
provenance.score_firewall: no composite analog score; distances and band memberships only

mars_panel_v3.note: the frozen benchmark; pre-specified, NOT pre-registered

lunar_panel_v2.note: same data was examined in v1 before the correction existed

regimes._note: The two regimes are NOT comparable to each other: different footprint, different supports, different bodies and different source resolutions. Nothing in this atlas pools across them.

verdict.one_axis_statement: The three declared axes span a single dimension at every support, over both the pool the frontier decides between (the seven Earth candidates) and the wider cross-body pool. Mean slope and mean 3x3 relief are mathematically the same measurement up to a direction factor bounded by 41% -- verified against the engine's own functions to floating point -- and the elevation standard deviation tracks them empirically. A Pareto frontier over these three is therefore a one-dimensional ordering and must not be reported as three lines of evidence.
verdict.what_this_does_not_mean: It does not make the lunar result wrong. It makes it smaller and more robust: a one-dimensional ordering is far more stable than a genuine three-dimensional frontier, which is consistent with the 6/6 ensemble and the 18/18 panel agreement.

uncertainty.note: Only the lunar DEM has a published error model, and only six of its 100 realisations were retrieved. The Earth side is treated as exact, which is a stated limitation rather than a finding.

reasons: 6 error realisations sampled while an ensemble claim is made; fewer than 30

questions.relative_ranking: Which candidate is closest, among the candidates tested?
questions.absolute_adequacy: Is any candidate inside the reference's own morphological variability at this scale, on a band the data can justify?
questions.evidence_sufficiency: Is the evidence enough to answer either of the other two for this comparison?

relative_ranking.question: Which candidate is closest, among the candidates tested?
relative_ranking.note: Relative to the candidate set tested. A unit can be closest here and still be far from the reference; that is what the adequacy part is for.
